name: Meshullam
overview: Meshullam was a male descendant of the tribe of Levi, specifically noted as a priestly figure due to his lineage. He is uniquely identified as the son of Ezra, placing him within the Aaronic priesthood. His role as a priest underscores his service in the religious life of Israel, emphasizing his Levitical heritage.
namesAndTitles: The name Meshullam means 'restitution' and is a proper name recorded in Nehemiah 12:13. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but it carries a meaningful Hebrew significance reflecting restoration or recompense.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Meshullam as the son of Ezra, establishing a clear familial link within the priestly line. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Meshullam's significance lies in his position as a priest descended from Aaron, serving during the period described in Nehemiah. His identification as the son of Ezra connects him to the leadership involved in the post-exilic restoration of Israel's worship practices. This highlights his role in maintaining the continuity of the Levitical priesthood and the spiritual renewal of the community.
